#### MRMPO Annual Listings of Obligations, FFY 2006–2009

This historical series documents federal transportation obligations in the Albuquerque Metropolitan Planning Area. The FFY 2006 tables identify projects, work phases, funding categories and federal authorizations, including a $48,193,701.21 annual total and comparisons with programmed amounts. The FFY 2007 tables add lead agencies, project identifiers, programmed and obligated amounts, differences and explanatory notes. Together they support research into how federal commitments supported Albuquerque traffic management, ABQ RIDE vehicles and facilities, bicycle programs and regional road improvements. Obligations are funding commitments, not proof of completed construction or final spending.

The preserved FFY 2008 and 2009 originals contain only one-page report cover sheets; they identify the reporting years and planning area but provide no project tables or obligation amounts. They remain available as limited components of this series, so these links do not establish a complete four-year funding comparison.

- FFY 2006: [project tables, archived PDF](https://files.abqinfo.com/transportation/transportation-plans/mrmpo-ffy-2006-annual-listing-obligations.pdf) · [Official MRCOG PDF](https://www.mrcog-nm.gov/DocumentCenter/View/3428/FFY-2006-Annual-Listing-of-Obligations-PDF)
- FFY 2007: [project tables, archived PDF](https://files.abqinfo.com/transportation/transportation-plans/mrmpo-ffy-2007-annual-listing-obligations.pdf) · [Official MRCOG PDF](https://www.mrcog-nm.gov/DocumentCenter/View/3432/FFY-2007-Annual-Listing-of-Obligations-PDF)
- FFY 2008: [cover sheet only, archived PDF](https://files.abqinfo.com/transportation/transportation-plans/mrmpo-ffy-2008-annual-listing-obligations.pdf) · [Official MRCOG PDF](https://www.mrcog-nm.gov/DocumentCenter/View/3421/FFY-2008-Annual-Listing-of-Obligations-PDF)
- FFY 2009: [cover sheet only, archived PDF](https://files.abqinfo.com/transportation/transportation-plans/mrmpo-ffy-2009-annual-listing-obligations.pdf) · [Official MRCOG PDF](https://www.mrcog-nm.gov/DocumentCenter/View/3422/FFY-2009-Annual-Listing-of-Obligations-PDF)

### Urban Enhancement Trust Fund 2010–2011

These three City records explain one Albuquerque cultural-funding cycle: how proposals were selected, the recommended budget and the organizations and activities proposed for support. The overview describes a public endowment established in 1983, an eleven-member citizens’ committee and a two-year review process coordinated with the General Obligation Program / Decade Plan. UETF projects require City Council approval rather than the voter approval required for general obligation bonds.

The committee reviewed 56 applications received in May 2008 for project quality, community impact and fiscal considerations. The recommended program allocated $887,892 to 41 projects, plus $15,982 in indirect/overhead costs, for a $903,874 total. The fourteen-page project list connects those allocations to named organizations, award amounts and intended activities: for example, $10,000 for 516 ARTS educational outreach, $46,000 for Albuquerque Youth Symphony concerts and $25,000 for ArtStreet public exhibits. Read together, the records show the selection framework, distribution of cultural support and intended public benefits; the recommendation documents do not establish final expenditures or completed outcomes.

- Program overview: [preserved original, archived PDF](https://files.abqinfo.com/city-data/capital-spending/cabq-urban-enhancement-trust-fund-program-overview-2010-2011.pdf) · [Official City PDF](https://www.cabq.gov/municipaldevelopment/documents/cip-documents/2009-go-bond-documents/uetf_2010-2011.pdf)
- Funding summary: [preserved original, archived PDF](https://files.abqinfo.com/city-data/capital-spending/cabq-urban-enhancement-trust-fund-funding-summary-2010-2011.pdf) · [Official City PDF](https://www.cabq.gov/municipaldevelopment/documents/cip-documents/2009-go-bond-documents/uetf_2010-2011_summary.pdf)
- Funded-project list: [preserved original, archived PDF](https://files.abqinfo.com/city-data/capital-spending/cabq-urban-enhancement-trust-fund-funded-projects-2010-2011.pdf) · [Official City PDF](https://www.cabq.gov/municipaldevelopment/documents/cip-documents/2009-go-bond-documents/uetf_2010-2011projects.pdf)

Collects nine official committee records tracing Chapter 28's adoption, section-by-section approval of Chapter 22, stormwater modeling discussions, and the appointment of subcommittees for Chapters 24, 25, and 26.

Collects seven official committee records documenting the planned division of the manual between the Integrated Development Ordinance and a technical standards manual, Chapter 23 subcommittee work, and Chapter 25 revisions.

Collects fifteen official committee records documenting completion of drainage standards, approval of survey, public-transit, parking, pedestrian, pavement, and building-permit provisions, and continuing review of network-connectivity and drafting standards.

Collects three official committee minutes plus the April 4 agenda preserved under the missing-minutes policy, documenting network-connectivity, intersection-design, construction-plan, and subdivision-compliance decisions and the final unfinished agenda items.

Collects five official committee records tracing the committee's launch, the voiding and re-adoption of its first chapter changes, and approval of the Development Process Manual preface and update procedure.

source_inspection: Fresh full public GETs matched exact inventory bytes for all 25 components and five existing annual masters. Text measured from these bytes. All pages of seven MRMPO/UETF PDFs visually inspected in contact sheets; original tables and narratives are legible and complete within each preserved object. FFY 2008/2009 contain cover sheets only.
dpm_review: Existing exhaustive September 13 source-page equivalence and visual QA applies to the same freshly verified five master hashes. Each of the 18 retired minute IDs occurs in the appropriate chronological annual master component list. Current annual descriptions already identify decisions/topics; no description rewrite is necessary. Annual compilations are ABQInfo browsing derivatives, not City publications or current standards. The 2018 missing-minutes agenda qualification remains unchanged.

### Urban Enhancement Trust Fund 2010–2011

These three City records explain one Albuquerque cultural-funding cycle: how proposals were selected, the recommended budget and the organizations and activities proposed for support. The overview describes a public endowment established in 1983, an eleven-member citizens’ committee and a two-year review process coordinated with the General Obligation Program / Decade Plan. UETF projects require City Council approval rather than the voter approval required for general obligation bonds.

The committee reviewed 56 applications received in May 2008 for project quality, community impact and fiscal considerations. The recommended program allocated $887,892 to 41 projects, plus $15,982 in indirect/overhead costs, for a $903,874 total. The fourteen-page project list connects those allocations to named organizations, award amounts and intended activities: for example, $10,000 for 516 ARTS educational outreach, $46,000 for Albuquerque Youth Symphony concerts and $25,000 for ArtStreet public exhibits. Read together, the records show the selection framework, distribution of cultural support and intended public benefits; the recommendation documents do not establish final expenditures or completed outcomes.

scope_assessment.substantive_rationale:
### Urban Enhancement Trust Fund 2010–2011

These three City records explain one Albuquerque cultural-funding cycle: how proposals were selected, the recommended budget and the organizations and activities proposed for support. The overview describes a public endowment established in 1983, an eleven-member citizens’ committee and a two-year review process coordinated with the General Obligation Program / Decade Plan. UETF projects require City Council approval rather than the voter approval required for general obligation bonds.

The committee reviewed 56 applications received in May 2008 for project quality, community impact and fiscal considerations. The recommended program allocated $887,892 to 41 projects, plus $15,982 in indirect/overhead costs, for a $903,874 total. The fourteen-page project list connects those allocations to named organizations, award amounts and intended activities: for example, $10,000 for 516 ARTS educational outreach, $46,000 for Albuquerque Youth Symphony concerts and $25,000 for ArtStreet public exhibits. Read together, the records show the selection framework, distribution of cultural support and intended public benefits; the recommendation documents do not establish final expenditures or completed outcomes.
